# Step 7: Instances

## Introduction

Add the real things your ontology describes.

An [instance](../../../../../docs/GLOSSARY.md#concept-instance) is one specific thing, like the cortado on your café's menu. Classes say what kinds of things exist. Instances are the things. You can read the full guide to this step in [Method](../../../../../docs/METHOD.md#step-7-instances).

## What you'll make

16 instances: eight ingredients, such as "Steamed whole milk", and eight menu items, each linked to what goes in it.

## Add ingredients

Run [`okb instance add`](../../../../../docs/CLI.md#cmd-instance-add) with `--of` for the class. Add the ingredients first, so the drinks can point at them:

```bash
okb instance add "Double shot" --of Coffee
okb instance add "Hot water" --of Water
okb instance add "Steamed whole milk" --of WholeMilk
okb instance add "Steamed half-and-half" --of HalfAndHalf
okb instance add "Milk foam" --of Foam
okb instance add "Chocolate syrup" --of Chocolate
okb instance add "Whipped cream" --of WhippedCream
okb instance add "Vanilla gelato" --of Gelato
```

```text
Added Double shot (a Coffee).

Added Hot water (a Water).

Added Steamed whole milk (a WholeMilk).

Added Steamed half-and-half (a HalfAndHalf).

Added Milk foam (a Foam).

Added Chocolate syrup (a Chocolate).

Added Whipped cream (a WhippedCream).

Added Vanilla gelato (a Gelato).
```

## Add the menu

Now add the menu items. Give only the values that aren't already fixed or defaulted. A cortado needs no ratio, because the class already fixes it:

```bash
okb instance add "House espresso" --of Espresso "contains=Double shot" "pourOrder=Shot into a warm cup"
okb instance add "Vertex cortado" --of Cortado "contains=Double shot,Steamed whole milk" "pourOrder=Shot first, then equal warm milk"
okb instance add "Vertex flat white" --of FlatWhite "contains=Double shot,Steamed whole milk" "pourOrder=Shot first, then thin milk"
okb instance add "Vertex cappuccino" --of Cappuccino "contains=Double shot,Steamed whole milk,Milk foam" "pourOrder=Shot, milk, then a cap of foam"
okb instance add "Vertex breve" --of Breve "contains=Double shot,Steamed half-and-half,Milk foam" "pourOrder=Shot, half-and-half, then foam"
okb instance add "Vertex mocha" --of Mocha "contains=Double shot,Chocolate syrup,Steamed whole milk" "pourOrder=Chocolate, shot, then milk"
okb instance add "Vertex affogato" --of Affogato "contains=Double shot,Vanilla gelato" "pourOrder=Gelato first, shot poured over"
```

```text
Added House espresso (an Espresso).
House espresso.contains = Double shot
House espresso.pourOrder = "Shot into a warm cup"

Added Vertex cortado (a Cortado).
Vertex cortado.contains = Double shot, Steamed whole milk
Vertex cortado.pourOrder = "Shot first, then equal warm milk"
Filled in default texture = "silky".

Added Vertex flat white (a FlatWhite).
Vertex flat white.contains = Double shot, Steamed whole milk
Vertex flat white.pourOrder = "Shot first, then thin milk"

Added Vertex cappuccino (a Cappuccino).
  Tip: Cappuccino has subclasses (Breve). Use the most specific class that fits.
Vertex cappuccino.contains = Double shot, Steamed whole milk, Milk foam
Vertex cappuccino.pourOrder = "Shot, milk, then a cap of foam"
Filled in default espressoToMilkRatio = 0.33.
Filled in default texture = "foamy".
Filled in default origin = "Italy".

Added Vertex breve (a Breve).
Vertex breve.contains = Double shot, Steamed half-and-half, Milk foam
Vertex breve.pourOrder = "Shot, half-and-half, then foam"
Filled in default espressoToMilkRatio = 0.33.
Filled in default texture = "foamy".
Filled in default origin = "USA".

Added Vertex mocha (a Mocha).
Vertex mocha.contains = Double shot, Chocolate syrup, Steamed whole milk
Vertex mocha.pourOrder = "Chocolate, shot, then milk"

Added Vertex affogato (an Affogato).
Vertex affogato.contains = Double shot, Vanilla gelato
Vertex affogato.pourOrder = "Gelato first, shot poured over"
```

## Add a link value

Some facts belong to the link itself. A macchiato has only a splash of foam, so say that on the link:

```bash
okb instance add "Vertex macchiato" --of Macchiato "contains=Double shot" "pourOrder=Shot, then a spoonful of foam"
okb link "Vertex macchiato" contains "Milk foam" amount=splash
```

```text
Added Vertex macchiato (a Macchiato).
Vertex macchiato.contains = Double shot
Vertex macchiato.pourOrder = "Shot, then a spoonful of foam"
Filled in default texture = "silky".

Linked (Vertex macchiato)-[:CONTAINS {amount: "splash"}]->(Milk foam)
```

## Read the output

Look at a drink and at an ingredient:

```bash
okb show "Vertex breve"
okb show "Milk foam"
```

```text
Vertex breve  Instance · i.vertex-breve-7fvaz3
  instance of    Breve

  Values
    espressoToMilkRatio 0.33
    texture            foamy
    pullVolumeMl       —
    pourOrder          Shot, half-and-half, then foam
    origin             USA
    contains           Double shot, Steamed half-and-half, Milk foam
    variationOf        Latte, Cappuccino (fixed by Breve)

Milk foam  Instance · i.milk-foam-ap9t4r
  instance of    Foam

  Values
    usedIn             Vertex cappuccino, Vertex breve, Vertex macchiato {amount: "splash"}
```

- **Values you didn't type.** The breve has `espressoToMilkRatio` and `texture` from the defaults on Cappuccino, and `origin` from its own default, USA. `variationOf` lists both Latte and Cappuccino, from the class.
- **[One edge, two views](../../../../../docs/learn/inverse-relationships.md).** "Milk foam" lists the drinks it goes into, though you only wrote `contains`. That's the inverse from step 6.

```text
Now on step 8. (To read a step's guide without moving: okb explain 8)

Step 8 of 8: Review against your questions, and iterate

  Goal: Stand back: check each competency question can be answered, run the full validator,
  review the judgment-only rules, record decisions, and go around again.
  Why it matters: The only real test of an ontology is whether it does the job it was built for.
  Expect to loop back to earlier steps.

Questions to answer
  • For each competency question: which classes, slots and instances answer it? Is anything
  missing?
  • For each answered question: would the ontology also answer the rest of its family, the same
  question about similar things and the questions next to it? Which of those are out of scope?
  • Is there anything in the ontology no question needs?
  • Would a domain expert agree with the hierarchy? Show it to one.
  • Which choices would surprise someone reusing this ontology? Are they recorded as design
  decisions?

You're done when
  ○ Every competency question is linked to what answers it
  ? Each question's family has been considered: wanted questions added, the rest recorded as out of scope
  ○ The whole ontology has no known mistakes
  ○ Every remaining issue is fixed or explained in a design decision
  ? Someone who knows the domain has looked at it

Tips
  • Iteration is part of the method, not a sign you went wrong.
  • Use the ontology-review skill for the judgment rules a script can't check.

In Ontology 101's wine example
  Ontology 101's own evolution example: Zinfandel starts under Red Wine, then 'white zinfandel'
  appears and the class has to be split into White Zinfandel and Red Zinfandel.

Commands
  okb cq link   okb validate --all   okb decision add   okb diagram
```

> **Common mistakes**
>
> - **Making an instance a class.** "Vertex cortado" is one cup on one menu. "Cortado" is a kind.
> - **Skipping a required link.** A drink needs at least one ingredient, so `okb validate` reports a drink without `contains`.

## Next step

You added eight ingredients and eight menu items. Next, you'll check the ontology against your questions and add two rules.
